description: The image displays two pie charts comparing error and success distributions across four categories — “Atomic Skill Fail,” “Correct,” “Reason Error,” and “Question Misunderstood” — likely representing performance breakdowns from the study “Laying the Foundation First: Investigating the Generalization from Atomic Skills to Complex Reasoning Tasks.” The left pie chart shows a dominant “Correct” category at 68.0% (medium teal), followed by “Atomic Skill Fail” at 12.0% (dark teal), “Reason Error” at 12.0% (light teal), and “Question Misunderstood” at 8.0% (white). The right pie chart presents a different distribution: “Correct” remains the largest segment at 55.0% (medium teal), followed by “Reason Error” at 21.0% (light teal), “Question Misunderstood” at 14.0% (white), and “Atomic Skill Fail” at 10.0% (dark teal). Both charts use a consistent color legend positioned above, with each slice labeled with its exact percentage. The visual comparison suggests a shift in error types between the two conditions or datasets represented, with the right chart showing a higher proportion of reasoning errors and misunderstood questions relative to atomic skill failures.
